scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: First, Perpetual futures (perps): no expiry; kept near spot by funding payments. Next, Positive funding: longs pay shorts (crowded longs). Negative: shorts pay longs. Then, Open interest (open interest): total open contracts. Rising open interest with rising price means leverage building. And finally, Liquidation data: bursts of forced closes.

scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Price +8% in a week, open interest +40%, funding at its highest in months: leverage is crowding into longs. That's a fragile setup (a drop could cascade) and, for Lesson 10.3, a funding-carry opportunity with a squeeze risk.
